What is MakerDAO?

MakerDAO is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that operates the Maker Protocol — the first and largest DeFi lending platform designed to issue DAI, the world's first decentralized stablecoin. Unlike centralized stablecoins backed by fiat currency, DAI is soft-pegged to the US Dollar and over-collateralized by cryptocurrency assets locked in smart contracts called Vaults.

The system was launched in 2017 by the Maker Foundation and later fully decentralized to token holders. Users generate DAI by depositing cryptocurrency collateral (such as ETH, WBTC, or USDC) into a Vault — formerly known as a CDP (Collateralized Debt Position). This collateral remains locked until the user repays the DAI debt plus an annual Stability Fee, at which point their collateral is released.

The protocol is governed by holders of the MKR token, who vote on critical parameters including stability fees, liquidation ratios, and which collateral types to support. When Vaults are under-collateralized and get liquidated, MKR tokens are minted and auctioned to cover the deficit — making MKR a "backstop" token that absorbs losses and aligns incentives between the protocol and its governors.

One of MakerDAO's most innovative features is the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), which allows any DAI holder to earn a variable interest rate simply by locking their DAI in a smart contract. This creates a direct, permissionless savings account with no minimums, no KYC, and funds accessible at any time — a revolutionary primitive in open finance.

💡 Key insight: DAI is not backed 1:1 by USD. It is backed by cryptocurrency worth significantly more than the DAI debt — currently ~410% globally. This over-collateralization is what protects DAI's peg during market downturns.

Accepted Collateral Types

Dai Savings Rate (DSR)

The Dai Savings Rate is a DeFi savings account built directly into the Maker Protocol. Any DAI holder can deposit their DAI into the DSR contract and earn a variable annual yield — currently around 3-5% APY. There are no minimum deposits, no lockup periods, and funds can be withdrawn at any time without penalty.

The DSR is funded by the stability fees collected from Vault users. A portion of every stability fee paid goes into the DSR pool, which is then distributed proportionally to all DAI depositors. This creates a direct connection between the borrowing and lending sides of the protocol.

Key Terms

CDP (Collateralized Debt Position)
The original name for a Vault in the Maker Protocol. A smart contract where users lock collateral to generate DAI debt.
Vault
The smart contract that holds a user's collateral and records their DAI debt. Formerly called a CDP.
Stability Fee
The annual interest rate charged on DAI debt. Paid in DAI (previously in MKR). Goes toward DSR payouts and protocol reserves.
Liquidation
When a Vault's collateral ratio falls below the minimum required ratio, any participant can liquidate it by repaying the DAI debt and claiming the collateral at a penalty discount (typically 13%).
Collateral Ratio
The ratio of collateral value to DAI debt. For example, a 200% ratio means your $20,000 ETH supports up to $10,000 DAI debt.
DAI Savings Rate (DSR)
The variable interest rate paid to DAI holders who deposit into the Maker Protocol's savings contract.
MKR Token
MakerDAO's governance token. MKR holders vote on protocol parameters, and MKR is used as a backstop — minted and sold to cover deficits during liquidations.
PETH (Pooled ETH)
An internal ERC-20 token representing a proportional share of the ETH pool used for Dai generation. Created during the SAI→DAI migration.
Dai
The decentralized, crypto-collateralized stablecoin issued by MakerDAO. Soft-pegged to $1 USD, over-collateralized by crypto assets.
Global Settlement
The emergency shutdown mechanism of the Maker Protocol. Closes all Vaults at fair prices and returns collateral to DAI and DSR depositors.

Risk Considerations

📉
Collateral Price Risk
If the value of collateral (ETH, WBTC) drops rapidly, Vaults can fall below the liquidation threshold before users can respond. A flash crash with no liquidity can result in significant collateral loss.
Medium Risk
⚖️
Governance Risk
MKR token holders control critical protocol parameters. A majority takeover could vote to reduce collateral requirements, change fees, or add risky collateral types — affecting all DAI holders.
Medium Risk
🔗
Depeg Risk
Although DAI has maintained its peg remarkably well, extreme market conditions could cause temporary depegs. The 2022 Terra/UST collapse increased scrutiny on all stablecoins. DAI's over-collateralization provides a buffer but isn't absolute protection.
Low-Medium Risk
💻
Smart Contract Risk
The Maker Protocol has been audited extensively and has a strong track record since 2017, but no smart contract is completely immune to exploits. A bug in the Vault or Oracle system could lead to loss of funds.
Low Risk
🔮
Oracle Risk
Maker relies on price oracles (primarily Chainlink) to determine collateral values. Oracle manipulation or failure could cause incorrect liquidations or under-collateralized positions.
Low Risk
🏛️
Regulatory Risk
As the largest DeFi stablecoin, MakerDAO faces regulatory attention. Enforcement actions or restrictive laws could affect DAI's usability, MKR's governance, or the protocol's operations.
Medium Risk
